findings.title: Executable shell scripts and wrapper aliases bypass the no-shell kernel
findings.diagnosis: loop-evidence executes an absolute executable whose first line is #!/bin/sh, env plus a symlink to sh, and a symlink to env plus sh and a script. Each independent case creates a marker, returns success, and changes both core and host heads. evidence.Capture also directly executes the shell script. RejectShell checks names only, does not inspect the script interpreter, does not resolve wrapper operands, and does not use the resolved wrapper identity. This violates architecture §§7.1 and 14. It requires no same-UID tampering with stored authority.

evidence.observation: Auditor suite under -race: four failing leaf cases (three loop shell entry points and direct Capture); 46 passing subtests plus standalone checks. No data race warnings. Unmodified product source; independent tests added only to copy.
Shell check uses executable names and argument basenames; no shebang inspection; wrapper operands not symlink-resolved. Successful Capture appends loop evidence.

fix.action: In internal/evidence/noshell.go, resolve the actual executable and any explicit command operand of supported wrappers. Reject shell interpreters reached by shebang (including env shebang forms) or symlinks before cmd.Run. Use that shared check for loop admission and Capture. For wrappers whose command operand cannot be identified safely, reject that wrapper at capture admission. Keep ordinary data arguments outside command-position checks.
fix.why: The kernel must classify the explicit execution entry point, including its interpreter and wrapper command, rather than trust a filename.

verification.method: Run TestAuditorFinal6ShellEntrypoints and TestAuditorFinal6CaptureShellScript with -race; include #!/bin/sh, #!/usr/bin/env sh, symlinked command operands and aliased env. Fingerprint both chains and marker before request.
verification.expected: All shell entry points refuse before marker creation and before either append; printf %s sh, a normal executable, and an allowed non-shell interpreter remain usable.

fix.tradeoffs: Shell-based verification scripts must be replaced with explicit non-shell checks. Wrapper command parsing needs an explicit supported grammar. This is not a general sandbox for arbitrary descendant processes.
fix.alternative: Use a verified allowlist of native executables and explicit non-shell interpreters, and refuse command wrappers and executable scripts until their entry points can be classified. This is simpler but reduces compatibility.

findings.title: A concurrent trusted core terminal append can precede loop check execution
findings.diagnosis: runHostLoopEvidence calls core Load, checks Terminal, then executes outside the core lock. The host lock serializes CLI transitions but does not serialize the trusted direct core append used in Gate B regression tests. An unchanged production path paused at its first snapshot Git call accepts a core ABORTED record. When resumed, it executes touch and creates the marker. Only afterwards does s.Append reject record chain discontinuity. No evidence or host record is accepted, but the check starts on a closed run. This fails A08 and the Gate B core/host ordering guarantee.

evidence.observation: Unmodified production path: Git helper pauses first snapshot Git call after core Load. Trusted bTerminal core append records ABORTED. Marker absent before release. After release the check creates marker; append fails record chain discontinuity; zero host records.
Loop releases core lock after Load and holds only host lock during execution; other host append paths hold both locks; Gate B already tests trusted concurrent core appends.

fix.action: Add a core-store transaction API that loads and appends under one existing core run lock. In runHostLoopEvidence, acquire host then core lock; check terminal/route, capture, retain output, append core evidence, and commit the host binding before releasing the core lock. Use a locked append callback; do not call the current locking Append recursively.
fix.why: The terminal check and execution admission must share the lock used by every trusted core append. A final optimistic predecessor check protects accepted records but cannot undo executed argv.

verification.method: Run TestAuditorFinal6CoreTerminalBeforeExecution under -race with the scheduling helper; also run TestAuditorFinal6TerminalAdmissionRace and an already-terminal/missing-run matrix.
verification.expected: If terminal authority commits first, no marker is created. If capture admission locks first, the terminal append waits until capture and binding finish. Valid open-run capture completes without deadlock.

verification.method: Repeat the schedule with an approved route rewind instead of ABORTED, and run all Gate B and Gate C tests, vet and dogfood.
verification.expected: A core revocation cannot land between authorization check and argv start; both chains remain coherent.

fix.tradeoffs: Holding the core lock across a check delays terminal and resolution writes; enforce bounded command duration and cancellation in the existing execution envelope. A transaction API is needed to avoid recursive-lock deadlock. Cross-chain crash recovery remains a separate concern; this finding does not claim new corruption.
fix.alternative: Introduce a durable execution-admission operation that every core authority-revoking writer must honor. This can reduce lock hold time but adds state and is larger than the existing host-then-core transaction pattern.

limitations: Fresh user-dispatched auditor context; no implementer conversation or prior Gate C verdict was read. Only status-stripped prior criteria were used before Phase 1. Authorized v7 contains incidental historical Gate A judgments; primary source/test comments also contain author interpretations, which were not treated as proof.

Repository was writable at the OS permission layer. Read-only was an audited behavior, not an OS-enforced mount. All audit writes and tests ran under /tmp/hma-gate-c-20261017-final6. Final HEAD, branch, status, binary diff SHA-256 and hashes of all 29 untracked files equal the start freeze. All 186 evaluated source/supplied-test files in audit copies match the source; see copy-source-verification.json.

Tests use synthetic host receipts, routes and approvals. No worker CLI, nested agent, model API or live production approval was invoked. External interfaces were inspected as contracts; no real end-to-end worker launch was performed.

Core terminal schedule uses the same trusted core Append fixture primitive as Gate B and a Git helper executable that only pauses and forwards unchanged arguments/output to /usr/bin/git. It does not alter production source. Host-lock-respecting CLI terminalization passes the separate positive control.
Gate D deferred behavior was not tested as implemented. Gate C does not certify bounded execution, positive criterion credit, reproduced finding dispositions or closure.
No approved Jev tool was exposed. Tool metadata search found none. Auditor/orchestrator decision fallback was recorded; no other model was presented as Jev.

Initial combined source outputs were truncated by the tool. Relevant authoritative excerpts and code were re-read in bounded calls; raw authoritative excerpts and source hashes are retained. Full TODO Gate C and scope §4a onward remain unread before this freeze.

Audit copies do not preserve real external side effects, production quotas or provider identity attestations. The trusted-host model excludes malicious same-UID forgery. Passing tests do not prove absence of all bugs.
